# knowledge_vault (SAMPLE FIXTURES)

Invented test content, not real policy. Replace with the real SOPs/catalog.
The first 7 notes are the Gate 3 seed set; 29 more synthetic notes were added on 2026-11-22 so the
250-question golden set (eval/) has enough distinct facts. RAGAS scores measure this synthetic corpus.

Note format (Gate 17): YAML frontmatter `id`, `domain`, `risk_tier`, `version`, optional `tenants`
(list of tenant_ids allowed to read; omit = all tenants), then Markdown body with `[[wikilinks]]`.

---
id: policy-access-control
domain: governance
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Access Control and Permission Tiers

System actions are grouped into three tiers.
TIER_1_READ: read records and search the knowledge base.
TIER_2_COMPUTE: run calculations and reports that do not change records.
TIER_3_MUTATE: change records, such as lot release, status changes, and form submission. Tier 3 always needs human approval, see [[policy-hitl-approval]].

Access is granted by role, never per person. Role assignments are reviewed every quarter by each department head.
Accounts are disabled within 24 hours of a person leaving the company. Accounts unused for 90 days are disabled automatically.
Every request carries a tenant ID, and a user can only see data for their own tenant.

# Quality Agreement Terms (tenant_acme only)

tenant_acme must be told about any Critical deviation affecting its lots within 24 hours.
Complaint investigations for tenant_acme close within 20 calendar days instead of 30.
tenant_acme receives a quarterly quality report covering deviations, complaints, and CAPAs for its products.
This note is visible only to tenant_acme.

id: policy-assistant-scope
domain: governance
risk_tier: 1
version: 1.0
---
# Assistant Scope

The assistant answers questions from the approved knowledge base and helps prepare records. It cites the notes it used.

It does not give medical, legal, or financial advice, and it does not answer questions outside manufacturing, quality, logistics, and governance. Such questions get a refusal.
If the knowledge base does not contain the answer, the assistant says so rather than guessing.

The assistant can read records (Tier 1) and run reports (Tier 2) directly. It can only request Tier 3 changes, which a human must approve, see [[policy-hitl-approval]] and [[policy-access-control]].
Personal data in user questions is redacted before processing, see [[policy-pii]].

id: policy-audit-trail
domain: governance
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Audit Trail

Every GMP computer system records an audit trail entry for each create, change, and delete. An entry holds who, what, when (UTC timestamp), the old value, the new value, and the reason.

Audit trails cannot be switched off or edited by any user, including administrators.
QA reviews the audit trail of each lot's electronic records as part of the batch record review, see [[sop-batch-record-review]].
System administrators' activity is reviewed separately every month.

The assistant writes an audit event for every tool call, including refused and expired Tier 3 requests.
Audit trails are kept as long as the records they describe, see [[policy-record-retention]].

id: sop-batch-record-review
domain: quality
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Batch Record Review

Every lot has an executed batch record (EBR). The batch record review is step 1 of lot release, see [[sop-lot-release]].

Production reviews the EBR first, within 2 working days of the end of manufacture. QA then performs an independent second review.
The reviewer checks that every step is signed and dated, every recorded value is within its limit, and every correction follows [[policy-data-integrity]].

Missing signatures, unexplained gaps, or values outside limits are review findings. A finding that cannot be explained by documentation is raised as a deviation, see [[sop-deviation]].
The review is complete only when all findings are closed and QA has signed the review page.
Target cycle time from end of manufacture to completed review is 5 working days.

id: sop-calibration
domain: maintenance
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Equipment Calibration

Every measuring instrument that affects product quality has a calibration ID in the format CAL-NNNN and a calibration interval.
Default intervals: balances every 6 months, temperature probes every 12 months, pH meters every 3 months.

A calibration label on the instrument shows the last and next due date. An instrument past its due date must not be used.
If an instrument fails calibration, maintenance tags it OUT OF SERVICE and QA assesses every result measured since the last passing calibration.
That impact assessment must be finished within 5 working days. Affected lots are placed on HOLD until it is finished.

Temperature loggers used for cold-chain storage are temperature probes and follow the 12-month interval, see [[sop-cold-chain]].

id: sop-capa
domain: quality
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA)

A CAPA is opened for every Major or Critical deviation, every confirmed out-of-specification result, and every complaint with a confirmed product defect.
Each CAPA has one owner, a due date, and an effectiveness check. Minor deviations need a CAPA only if the same root cause recurs three times within 12 months.

The CAPA plan must be approved by QA within 10 working days of the root-cause report, see [[sop-root-cause]].
Corrective actions fix the detected problem; preventive actions stop it happening on other lines, products, or sites.

Due dates: Critical CAPAs are due within 30 calendar days, Major CAPAs within 60 calendar days.
A due date can be extended once, by up to 30 days, with a written justification approved by the QA manager.

The effectiveness check runs 90 days after the last action is closed. If the problem recurs during those 90 days, the CAPA is reopened.
A deviation can only be closed after its CAPA is approved, see [[sop-deviation]].

id: sop-change-control
domain: quality
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Change Control

Any change to an approved process, specification, equipment, supplier, or computer system needs a change request (CR) before it is made.

Each CR is classified Minor, Moderate, or Major. Major changes need approval from the Change Control Board, which meets every Tuesday. Minor and Moderate changes are approved by the QA manager.
A Major change to a validated process also needs revalidation before the first lot made under it can be released.

Emergency changes may be made before approval only to protect product or patient safety. They must be documented within 24 hours and approved retrospectively within 5 working days.
Implementing a change without an approved CR is a deviation, see [[sop-deviation]]. Changes to suppliers also follow [[sop-supplier-qualification]].

id: sop-cleaning-validation
domain: manufacturing
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Cleaning and Line Clearance

Shared equipment is cleaned between products using a validated cleaning procedure.
The acceptance limit for carry-over is 10 ppm of the previous product's active ingredient, or 1/1000 of its lowest therapeutic dose, whichever is lower.

Cleaned equipment carries a CLEAN status label valid for 72 hours. After 72 hours it must be cleaned again before use.
Before a new lot starts, the operator performs a line clearance: remove all materials, labels, and documents from the previous lot, and a second person verifies it.

A failed swab test is a deviation, see [[sop-deviation]]. The cleaning procedure is revalidated whenever a new product is added to shared equipment, under [[sop-change-control]].

id: sop-cold-chain
domain: logistics
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Cold-Chain Storage

Temperature-sensitive products are stored between 2 °C and 8 °C.
Any excursion above 8 °C for more than 30 minutes is a deviation, see [[sop-deviation]].
Temperature loggers are read before a cold-chain lot is released, see [[sop-lot-release]].

id: sop-complaint-handling
domain: quality
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Customer Complaint Handling

Every complaint is logged within 1 working day of receipt with a complaint ID in the format CMP-NNNNNN.

Complaints are triaged as safety-related or quality-only. A safety-related complaint is escalated to the Head of Quality the same day and assessed for recall, see [[sop-recall]].
Investigation of a quality-only complaint must be completed within 30 calendar days.

The investigation checks the retained sample of the lot, the batch record, and any open deviations against the lot.
A complaint with a confirmed product defect requires a CAPA, see [[sop-capa]]. The customer receives a written response when the investigation closes.
Complaint data is trended monthly. Three complaints of the same type for one SKU in a quarter trigger a review by the product owner.

---
id: policy-data-integrity
domain: governance
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Data Integrity (ALCOA+)

All GMP records must be ALCOA+: Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate, plus Complete, Consistent, Enduring, and Available.

Paper corrections use a single line through the old value, so it stays readable, with the new value, initials, date, and a reason. Correction fluid and overwriting are forbidden.
Electronic records keep a full audit trail of every change, see [[policy-audit-trail]].

Shared user accounts are forbidden on GMP systems. Each person signs with their own credentials.
A data-integrity breach, such as backdating a record, is always classified at least Major, see [[sop-deviation]].

---
id: sop-deviation
domain: quality
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Deviation Handling

A deviation is any departure from an approved procedure or specification.
Deviations are classified Minor, Major, or Critical within 24 hours of detection.
Critical deviations place every affected lot on HOLD immediately.
A deviation is closed only after root-cause analysis and CAPA approval.
Related: [[sop-lot-release]].

---
id: sop-environmental-monitoring
domain: manufacturing
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Environmental Monitoring

Production rooms are graded A to D. Grade A is the cleanest and is used for aseptic filling.

Viable air samples are taken in every Grade A and B room during every shift, and in Grade C rooms weekly. Grade D rooms are sampled monthly.
Each result is compared with an alert level and an action level. An alert-level result triggers extra sampling for 3 consecutive days. An action-level result is a deviation, see [[sop-deviation]].

Room differential pressure is logged continuously. A pressure drop lasting more than 15 minutes in a Grade A or B room stops aseptic work in that room.
Any lot filled in a room during an action-level excursion is placed on HOLD until QA completes an impact assessment.

---
id: globex-shipping
domain: logistics
risk_tier: 1
version: 1.0
tenants: [tenant_globex]
---
# Shipping Exceptions (tenant_globex only)

tenant_globex accepts lots with at least 4 months of remaining shelf life, instead of the standard 6 months, under its written agreement with us.
Cold-chain deliveries to tenant_globex must arrive within 36 hours instead of 48.
Globex delivery issues are reported to the Globex logistics desk within 4 hours.
This note is visible only to tenant_globex.

---
id: policy-hitl-approval
domain: governance
risk_tier: 3
version: 1.0
---
# Human Approval for Tier 3 Actions

Any action that changes records (lot release, status change, form submission) is Tier 3.
The assistant never executes Tier 3 actions itself. It creates a PENDING_APPROVAL request and
an authorized reviewer approves or rejects it. Requests not decided within 24 hours expire as REJECTED.

---
id: sop-in-process-checks
domain: manufacturing
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# In-Process Checks

In-process checks (IPCs) confirm a lot stays within limits while it is being made. All IPC results are step 2 of lot release, see [[sop-lot-release]].

Standard IPCs for tablets: weight every 15 minutes, hardness every 30 minutes, and disintegration once per hour.
Standard IPCs for liquids: pH and fill volume every 20 minutes.

A single result outside limits stops the line. The operator retests once with a fresh sample. If the retest is also outside limits, the shift supervisor raises a deviation, see [[sop-deviation]].
An IPC instrument must have a valid calibration on the day of use, see [[sop-calibration]]. Results from an instrument found out of calibration are invalid back to its last passing calibration.

---
id: sop-incoming-inspection
domain: procurement
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Incoming Material Inspection

Every incoming delivery is placed in QUARANTINE on receipt and cannot be used until QC releases it.

QC checks the delivery against the purchase order, the supplier's certificate of analysis, and the label. Active ingredients are identity-tested on every container.
Other materials from approved suppliers are sampled using the square-root rule: sample √n + 1 containers, where n is the number of containers delivered.
Materials from a supplier on conditional status are fully tested, see [[sop-supplier-qualification]].

Released material gets a green RELEASED label. Rejected material gets a red REJECTED label and is returned or destroyed within 30 days.
Cold-chain materials are checked for temperature excursions during transport before they are moved into storage, see [[sop-cold-chain]].

---
id: sop-label-control
domain: manufacturing
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Label Control

Printed labels are controlled materials. They are issued to the line by count and every unused label is counted back at the end of the lot.

The label reconciliation must balance exactly: labels issued = labels applied + labels returned + labels destroyed. Any difference is a deviation, see [[sop-deviation]].
Each label shows the product name, SKU, lot number, and expiry date. Lot numbers follow [[catalog-lot-numbering]].

Label artwork changes go through [[sop-change-control]]. Obsolete labels are destroyed under witness on the day a new version is approved.
A label mix-up found after release is a Critical deviation and is assessed for recall, see [[sop-recall]].

---
id: catalog-lot-numbering
domain: catalog
risk_tier: 1
version: 1.0
---
# Lot Numbering

Lot numbers use the format LOT-NNNNN: the prefix LOT-, then exactly five digits, zero padded. For example, lot 44 is written LOT-00044.

Lot numbers are assigned in sequence by the manufacturing system when the batch record is opened, and are never reused, even if the lot is rejected.
One lot is made from one SKU on one line in one continuous run. A lot that is split for packaging keeps its lot number, with suffixes -A, -B, and so on for each split.
The lot status lifecycle is: QUARANTINE → RELEASED, or QUARANTINE → REJECTED. A released lot can later move to HOLD or RECALLED. See [[sop-lot-release]].
SKU formats are defined in [[catalog-sku]].

---
id: sop-lot-release
domain: quality
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Lot Release Safety Protocol

Every production lot (format LOT-NNNNN) must pass a safety verification before release.
Verification requires: (1) batch record review complete, (2) all in-process checks within limits,
(3) no open deviations against the lot, and (4) QA sign-off recorded in the state store.

A lot in status HOLD cannot be shipped. Releasing a lot is a Tier 3 mutation and requires
reviewer approval, see [[policy-hitl-approval]]. Open deviations are handled per [[sop-deviation]].
Cold-chain lots also need a temperature log check, see [[sop-cold-chain]].

---
id: sop-oos
domain: quality
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Out-of-Specification Results

An out-of-specification (OOS) result is a test result outside its approved specification.

Phase I is a laboratory investigation by the analyst and the lab supervisor, completed within 3 working days. It checks for calculation errors, instrument problems, and sample preparation errors.
If Phase I finds a clear laboratory error, the result is invalidated and the test is repeated.
If not, Phase II, a full investigation including manufacturing, starts and must finish within 20 working days.

Retesting to "test into compliance" is forbidden. A confirmed OOS result means the lot is rejected unless QA documents a scientific justification.
Every confirmed OOS needs root-cause analysis and a CAPA, see [[sop-root-cause]] and [[sop-capa]].

---
id: policy-pii
domain: governance
risk_tier: 1
version: 1.0
---
# Personal Data Handling

Email addresses, phone numbers, and national ID numbers are redacted before any processing.
Raw personal data is never stored in logs, caches, or databases.

---
id: catalog-product-families
domain: catalog
risk_tier: 1
version: 1.0
---
# Product Families

SKU-099 (Cardiolex 5 mg injection) is refrigerated, stored between 2 °C and 8 °C, with a shelf life of 18 months.
SKU-120 (Dermasol cream 50 g) is shelf-stable at room temperature, with a shelf life of 36 months.
SKU-145 (Pulmovent inhaler) is stored at room temperature, with a shelf life of 24 months.
SKU-210 (Glycobal 500 mg tablets) is stored at room temperature, with a shelf life of 48 months.
SKU-305 (Vaxigen vaccine 0.5 mL) is refrigerated and must never be frozen, with a shelf life of 12 months.

Refrigerated SKUs follow [[sop-cold-chain]]. Room-temperature SKUs follow [[sop-warehouse-storage]].
SKU-077 was discontinued in 2024; its number is kept and never reassigned, see [[catalog-sku]].

---
id: sop-qa-signoff
domain: quality
risk_tier: 3
version: 1.0
---
# QA Sign-Off

QA sign-off is step 4 of lot release, see [[sop-lot-release]]. Only a Qualified Person (QP) may sign off a lot.

Before signing, the QP confirms that the batch record review is complete, all in-process checks are within limits, there are no open deviations against the lot, and, for cold-chain lots, the temperature log is acceptable.
The sign-off is recorded in the state store with the QP's user ID and a timestamp. It is a Tier 3 action and goes through [[policy-hitl-approval]].

A QP may not sign off a lot they personally manufactured or reviewed in production.
A sign-off can be revoked only by the Head of Quality. Revoking a sign-off puts the lot on HOLD.

---
id: sop-recall
domain: quality
risk_tier: 3
version: 1.0
---
# Product Recall

A recall removes distributed product from the market. It is decided by the Recall Committee, chaired by the Head of Quality.

Recall classes: Class I (risk of serious harm or death), Class II (risk of temporary or reversible harm), Class III (unlikely to cause harm).
The regulator is notified within 24 hours for a Class I recall and within 72 hours for Class II and Class III.

Distribution records must allow every customer who received the lot to be identified within 4 hours, see [[sop-shipping]].
Initiating a recall changes lot status to RECALLED and is a Tier 3 action, see [[policy-hitl-approval]].
A mock recall is run once a year for one randomly chosen lot to test the 4-hour trace.

---
id: policy-record-retention
domain: governance
risk_tier: 1
version: 1.0
---
# Record Retention

Batch records and QA sign-off records are kept for 1 year after the lot's expiry date, or 5 years after release, whichever is longer.
Shipping and distribution records are kept for 5 years.
Training records are kept for the length of employment plus 10 years.
Complaint and recall records are kept for 10 years.

Records may be destroyed only after the retention period ends and QA approves the destruction list.
Records under a legal hold are never destroyed, whatever their retention period.
Electronic records must stay readable for the whole retention period, including after a system is retired.

---
id: sop-returns
domain: logistics
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Returned Goods

Returned product is placed in QUARANTINE on arrival and is never put straight back into saleable stock.

Returned goods can be returned to stock only if all of these are true: the packaging is unopened, the product stayed within its storage conditions the whole time, and more than 12 months of shelf life remain.
Cold-chain products can never be returned to stock, because their storage history outside our control cannot be verified. They are destroyed.

The decision to return to stock is made by QA and recorded against the original lot number.
Product returned because of a complaint is handled under [[sop-complaint-handling]] and kept as evidence until that complaint is closed.

---
id: sop-root-cause
domain: quality
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Root-Cause Analysis

Root-cause analysis (RCA) is required for every Major and Critical deviation and every confirmed out-of-specification result, see [[sop-oos]].
The RCA report is due within 15 working days of deviation classification.

Approved methods are the 5 Whys, the fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram, and fault-tree analysis. Critical deviations must use at least two methods.
The RCA team includes the process owner, a QA representative, and at least one operator from the affected shift.

"Human error" is not accepted as a root cause on its own. The report must state why the error was possible, for example unclear instructions or missing training, see [[sop-training]].
When no root cause can be found, the report is labelled "root cause not determined" and the CAPA must include extra monitoring for 6 months, see [[sop-capa]].

---
id: sop-shipping
domain: logistics
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Shipping and Distribution

Only lots with status RELEASED can be shipped. A lot on HOLD, in QUARANTINE, or RECALLED is blocked by the warehouse system.

Orders are picked first-expiry, first-out (FEFO). A lot with less than 6 months of remaining shelf life is not shipped unless the customer agrees in writing.
Cold-chain shipments use validated insulated shippers with a temperature logger in each shipper, and must arrive within 48 hours, see [[sop-cold-chain]].

Each shipment record stores the lot number, customer, quantity, and dispatch date. These records support the 4-hour trace in [[sop-recall]] and are kept per [[policy-record-retention]].

---
id: catalog-sku
domain: catalog
risk_tier: 1
version: 1.0
---
# SKU Catalog Conventions

Product SKUs use the format SKU-NNN (three digits, zero padded), for example SKU-099.
SKU-099 is a refrigerated product and follows [[sop-cold-chain]].
SKU-120 is shelf-stable at room temperature.
Discontinued SKUs keep their number and are never reassigned.

---
id: sop-stability-testing
domain: quality
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Stability Testing

Stability studies confirm a product stays within specification for its full shelf life.

The first three commercial lots of every new product enter the stability program. After that, one lot per SKU per year is added.
Long-term samples are tested at 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, and 24 months, then yearly until the end of shelf life.
Refrigerated products are stored at 5 °C ± 3 °C for long-term testing. Room-temperature products are stored at 25 °C ± 2 °C and 60% relative humidity.

A stability result outside specification is an out-of-specification result, see [[sop-oos]], and is reported to the Head of Quality within 2 working days.
Shelf life can only be extended after real-time data covers the new period, and the extension is a change under [[sop-change-control]].

---
id: sop-supplier-qualification
domain: procurement
risk_tier: 2
version: 1.0
---
# Supplier Qualification

Only approved suppliers may supply materials that touch the product. Approved suppliers are listed in the Approved Supplier List (ASL).

A new supplier is approved after a questionnaire, a quality agreement, and, for active ingredients and primary packaging, an on-site audit.
Approved suppliers are re-audited every 3 years, or every year if they had a Critical audit finding.

Suppliers are scored quarterly on on-time delivery and rejected deliveries. A supplier with more than 3 rejected deliveries in 12 months is moved to conditional status and every delivery gets full testing, see [[sop-incoming-inspection]].
Removing a supplier from the ASL or adding a new one is a change under [[sop-change-control]].

---
id: acme-escalation
domain: quality
risk_tier: 1
version: 1.0
tenants: [tenant_acme]
---
# Escalation Contacts (tenant_acme only)

Quality escalations for tenant_acme go to the on-call QA lead through the escalation queue.
This note is visible only to tenant_acme and is used to test tenant filtering.

---
id: sop-training
domain: governance
risk_tier: 1
version: 1.0
---
# Training and Qualification

Staff may perform a GMP task only after training on the current version of its procedure is recorded.

New procedures and revised procedures must be trained before their effective date. The training window is 14 days.
Operators are requalified on aseptic technique every 6 months. Qualified Persons complete 20 hours of continuing education per year.

Training records are kept for the length of employment plus 10 years, see [[policy-record-retention]].
A task performed by someone without a valid training record is a deviation, see [[sop-deviation]]. RCA reports that cite human error must check the training record, see [[sop-root-cause]].

---
id: sop-warehouse-storage
domain: logistics
risk_tier: 1
version: 1.0
---
# Warehouse Storage

Room-temperature products are stored between 15 °C and 25 °C with relative humidity below 60%.
Refrigerated products are stored per [[sop-cold-chain]].

Warehouse locations are mapped for temperature every 2 years and after any change to the building or HVAC system.
QUARANTINE, REJECTED, and RECALLED stock is kept in a physically separate, locked area. Only warehouse staff with the quarantine role can move stock in or out of it.

A full stock count is done once a year. A count difference above 0.5% for any SKU is investigated as a deviation, see [[sop-deviation]].
